purpose: Two short Spurgeon quotations on faith and receiving grace.

defaults.author: C. H. Spurgeon
defaults.rightsBasis: 1886 edition, public domain in the USA. Wording matched to stored OCR; page-scan verification pending.
defaults.reviewNote: Read in surrounding source context. Spurgeon's prose, not Scripture. Confirm against page images before publication; use KJV for accompanying Bible text.

entries.title: Receive the Offered Treasure
entries.text: He who may have a treasure simply by his grasping it will be foolish indeed if he remains poor.
entries.slideText: He who may have a treasure simply by his grasping it will be foolish indeed if he remains poor.
entries.sourceLocator: How May Faith Be Illustrated?, printed page 51
entries.recommendedUse: A metaphor for receiving grace in Christ, not a promise of financial wealth.

entries.title: Faith Begins with Knowledge
entries.text: Faith is not a blind thing; for faith begins with knowledge.
entries.slideText: Faith is not a blind thing; for faith begins with knowledge.
entries.sourceLocator: Faith, What Is It?, printed page 47
entries.recommendedUse: Introduce the chapter's explanation of knowing, believing, and trusting the gospel.
